Saint Petersburg. The second-largest city in Russia, located on the Gulf of Finland at the mouth of the Neva River. Founded in seventeen oh-three by Peter the Great as a deliberate attempt to create a window to the West, it served as the capital of the Russian Empire for over two hundred years.

Peter the Great founded Saint Petersburg in seventeen oh-three deliberately moving power from Moscow to establish closer ties with Western Europe and assert Russian modernization. The city was built on swampy, inhospitable terrain at enormous human cost. Thousands of serfs died in its construction, but it became one of Europe's most beautiful and planned cities.

Saint Petersburg became the intellectual and cultural heart of the Russian Empire, producing literary giants like Fyodor Dostoevsky and Alexander Pushkin and musical masters like Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky. The Winter Palace, the imperial residence of the Russian tsars, was the center of political power for the empire. It is now home to the Hermitage Museum, one of the world's greatest art collections, housing imperial collections of unparalleled scope.

The city's neoclassical architecture, designed by Italian and Russian architects like Bartolomeo Rastrelli, exemplifies eighteenth-century imperial grandeur and remains largely preserved. This architectural legacy gives the city a distinctive character among the world's great capitals.

During World War I, the city was renamed Petrograd due to anti-German sentiment. It was the epicenter of the Russian Revolution of nineteen seventeen. The Winter Palace was stormed by revolutionaries in October nineteen seventeen, marking a turning point in world history. Following the revolution, the Soviet Union renamed the city Leningrad from nineteen twenty-four to nineteen ninety-one.

During World War II, Saint Petersburg endured a brutal nine hundred-day siege. The population was devastated by starvation and bombardment, yet the city survived and eventually recovered. After the Soviet Union dissolved, the city reclaimed its original name and its status as a repository of Russian imperial culture.

Today Saint Petersburg stands as an icon of imperial ambition and cultural refinement, a living museum of Russian history. Its palaces, museums, and artistic masterworks continue to attract visitors from around the world, preserving the legacy of Peter the Great's grand vision and Russia's imperial past.
